answer: A public registry acts as a beacon: each agent must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for paid tasks. Like bees seeking nectar, attackers may spawn a plume of identities, but each one needs its own deposit; 10,000 fakes tie up a million tokens for a month. The registry checks deposits on-chain and assigns each deposit to one identity, so splitting accounts cannot reuse the same collateral.
